messages.subject: Binomial regression with random effects
parts:
I am new to stan. I need to do some calculations within my stan file and I running into problems. I am trying to fit the following model

Y_ij ~ Binom(n_ij,pij)
logit(pij) ~ beta + bi + bij_i
where
(bi1,....,biJ_i) ~ N(0,I)
bi ~ N(rho*sum(bij_i),sigma^2*(1-rho^2*J))

I need to include the constraint for rho in order for the normal distribution to be well defined.

This is my code

data {
  int<lower=0> N;                   // number of observations
  int<lower=0> NS;                  // number of subjects
  int<lower=0> NP[NS];              // number of partnerships
  int<lower=0> cNS[NS];             // cumulative number of partnerships
  int<lower=0> y[N];                // number of insertive acts
  int<lower=0> n[N];                // number of acts
  int<lower=0,upper=1> circum[N];   // explanatory variable: circumcision
  real age[N];                      // explanatory variable: age - mean(age)
  int<lower=0> id[N];               // id variable
}

parameters {
  real alpha0;
  real alpha1;
  real alpha2;  
  real<lower=0> sigma2;         // Variance
  real b[N];                    // Random effect - partnership level
  real bb[NS];            // Random effect - partner level   
  real<lower=-0.2,upper=0.2> rho;
}

transformed parameters {
 real<lower=0> sigma;
 sigma <- sqrt(sigma2);
}

model
{
  real p[N];   // Template
  real a[NS];                   // Template sum
  for(k in 1:N){
   b[k] ~ normal(0,sigma);
  }
  for(s in 1:cNS[1]){
    a[1] <- a[1] + b[s];
  }         
  for(j in 2:NS){
    for(s in (cNS[j-1]+1):cNS[j]) a[j] <- a[j] + b[s];
  }
  for(h in 1:NS) bb[h] ~ normal(rho*a[h],sigma*sigma*(1-rho*rho*NP[h]));
  for(i in 1:N){
    p[i]  <- inv_logit(alpha0 + alpha1 * circum[i] + alpha2 * age[i]  +  bb[id[i]] + b[i]);
    y[i]  ~ binomial_logit(n[i],p[i]);   
  }
}

The error that I get is (Thanks in advance for any suggestion)

> model2  <- stan(file="logistic_model_v2.stan",data=windat5,chains=3,iter=2000)

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'logistic_model_v2' NOW (CHAIN 1).
 [1] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                             
 [2] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                         
 [3] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                       
 [4] "Exception thrown at line 45: stan::math::normal_log: Location parameter is 1.#QNAN, but must be finite!"                              
 [5] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
 [6] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                             
 [7] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                             
 [8] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                         
 [9] "Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts. "                                                                           
[10] " Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model."                                
[1] "error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done"

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Binomial regression with random effects
parts:
The error message says the problem is at line 45 of your code, so
I'd suggest looking at the arguments to the normal there and
working backwards to make sure they're what you think they should
be. You can use print() statements.

Just looking at your code quickly, there are a few problems:

You need to initialize the variable a before using it.

And you don't want to do both inv_logit and binomial_logit.
The binomial_logit has the inv_logit built-in.

Given that you define sigma2, you might as well use
that as (sigma * sigma) in the model block. All of those sampling
statements can be vectorized.

- Bob
